validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + SPEC: this row has no gem.wiki page (open-web/source-reread from scratch, per scope note). GEM's own cited source is the EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF (egyptoil-gas.com). A full-text search of that PDF for 'Qena' only turns up the word as a governorate name in unrelated household-gas-connection program text (pdftotext hits at lines ~646/686) -- NOT evidence this pipeline is unsourced, because (per this cohort's standing method) this whole batch of 40 rows was digitized visually off the GASCO national-grid wall-map printed on p.35 of that same report (PDF page 19 of 36), and that page is almost entirely a raster map with no OCR-able pipeline-name text. I rendered p.35 at 400dpi (pdftoppm) and visually inspected the Qena/Qus/Luxor corridor. Finding: the map shows a teal 'Regas' node labeled 'Qena P.S' immediately west/south of a second teal 'Regas' node labeled 'Qena' (the city gate, next to the Qena/Queft industrial-area icon), joined by a short green pipe segment carrying the rotated annotation '26"- 8 Km' running right along that exact segment. This is an EXACT match to GEM's row: Qena P.S -> Qena, Length=8.00 km, Diameter=26 in. The segment is drawn in the map's light-green 'EXISTING P/L' color (confirmed against the map's own legend box, which reads: green=EXISTING P/L, red=UNDER CONS. P/L, blue=UNDER STUDY P/L) -- not the red 'under construction' or blue 'under study' colors used elsewhere on the same map -- which independently corroborates Status=operating (and, by extension, PipelineType=transmission: it is a metered pressure-station-to-city-gate feeder off the national trunk grid, the same convention this cohort uses for the other short PS-to-facility rows, e.g. P8072/P8073). Both endpoints sit in Qena Governorate, consistent with StartState/Province=Qena, EndState/Province=Qena, StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Egypt. FuelSource=Gas is self-evident (this is GASCO's natural-gas national grid map). No duplicate risk: checked against the DUPLICATE watchlist and the full 40-row roster -- nothing else in-scope touches Qena, and the map draws this 8 km/26in spur as visually and dimensionally distinct from the separate north-south trunk corridor that runs through the same area at 30in/392km (Qus-Luxor label) and which GulfPub's global gas layer separately carries as a 242 km/30in 'South Valley Gas Pipeline' spanning lat 24.10-26.33N (i.e. the trunk already tracked elsewhere, almost certainly under GEM's existing P0477 South Valley network row per the country note, not this row). CAVEAT (why this is 'confirmed (caveat)' and not a clean 'confirmed'): this map is the SAME document GEM already cites for every field on this row -- reading its map panel is a different reading of one source, not a second independent one, so per the >=2-independent-sources near-requirement this is only a single strong (tier=medium) confirmation. I attempted to find a second, genuinely independent source (GASCO/EGAS site directly, Wikipedia, engineering-contractor project lists, Arabic press) but this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before I could run any queries, and duckduckgo/bing were unreachable via WebFetch (CAPTCHA / no rendered results); the two other registered scrape sources in this repo (OSM Egypt-gas: 21 features, all in the Nile Delta/north coast, none within 0.3 deg of Qena; GulfPub gas: only the unrelated 242km trunk touches the area) have no coverage of this specific short spur. Recommend a fresh session retry an open-web/Arabic-press search for independent confirmation of the Qena P.S-Qena tie-in; nothing here contradicts the sheet, so no value change is warranted in the meantime.
